usage: Code health guardrails for handyboy, applied by `cs review`, `cs check`, `cs delta` and the CodeScene PR gates. Every rule set below is a guardrail against coding-agent entropy: this repository is authored entirely by coding agents, and the harness they run inside is checked in with them - `.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, .agents/hooks.json, `.factory/settings.json`, the `.entire/` session config, `.github/hooks/entire.json`, and the two hook plugins those installers generate (`.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`, `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts`). The failure modes these rules catch are therefore agent failure modes: a browser-agent graph that accretes one more branch until neither role can be read, a run manager whose launch path is 192 lines of interleaved awaits, a page-action function that grows a fourth nested guard, a test suite that is copied rather than written. Every rule set encodes a code-level metric only - no set keys off a person, a team or a review route - and evaluation is first-match-wins from top to bottom, so the list is ordered narrowest-glob-first: the two generated Entire hook plugins first, then the four test globs, then one rule set per architectural layer of the extension and the native host, and the broad `**/*` catch-all last so that any directory a future change introduces starts under the full guardrail. A weight of 1.0 is the framework default and means the rule counts; 0.0 disables the rule for the matched files and is used only for code this repository does not author.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: Generated, not authored. `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` is the OpenCode plugin that `entire enable --agent opencode` writes; its own header lines 2-3 read `Auto-generated by `entire enable --agent opencode`` and `Do not edit manually - changes will be overwritten on next install.` It is 585 physical lines / 378 lines of code by the measurement in .codescene/README.md and scores 5.83 with the framework profile: `EntirePlugin:Plugin.event` (lines 400-583) is a 143-code-line hook dispatcher at cc 84 with five bumps, plus `Primitive Obsession` and `String Heavy Function Arguments`. All 23 rules are weighted 0.0 so the generated plugin is never a refactoring target. Improving its event handler would produce a diff the next `entire enable` silently discards, and the architecture it would 'improve' is the Entire CLI's, not this repository's.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: Generated by `entire enable --agent pi`, with the same two header lines naming the installer and forbidding edits. `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts` is 147 physical lines / 94 lines of code, forwards Pi lifecycle events to `entire hooks pi <event>`, and its `ENTIRE_CMD` constant is replaced at install time - so even a cosmetic edit is undone by the installer. It scores 10.0 today. All 23 rules are 0.0 so that a future Entire release cannot turn a generated extension into a refactoring task, and so that any hand edit inside `.pi/extensions/` shows up as a deliberate, reviewable decision rather than as a health improvement.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The native host's own vitest suite: 16 `*.test.ts` suites listed by `host/vitest.config.ts` `include: ['test/**/*.test.ts']`, plus the two support modules that live beside them - `host/test/harness.ts` (a fake native-messaging channel, 80 lines of code) and `host/test/setup.ts` (the per-suite setup file the config names). These cover the wire contract in `docs/host-protocol.md`: framing, dispatcher routing, secret resolution and retry, run-log appends, readiness and the dev trigger. `host/test/secrets.test.ts` and `host/test/dispatcher.test.ts` are each touched in 4 of the 21 commits this repository has, which makes them the hottest files in the host half - a test is frequently the hottest file in an agent-authored repository.

rule_sets.rules_doc: The compliant test profile: Bumpy Road Ahead, Deep, Nested Complexity, Complex Method, Code Duplication, Large Assertion Blocks, Duplicated Assertion Blocks and Lines of Code in a Single File stay at 1.0, because they describe exactly what an agent does to a passing suite - copy a block of asserts, add a nested branch to a fake, let a module grow until the case it protects cannot be found. Exactly three rules are 0.0 and only these three: `Low Cohesion` is a class-field metric and these suites are class-per-behaviour with module-level fakes; `Primitive Obsession` and `String Heavy Function Arguments` describe typed-model discipline in application code, and a fake channel that takes a JSON string and a method name is the correct test double, not a smell.
rule_sets.thresholds_doc: `file_lines_of_code_for_warning` 500, applied to every test rule set in this file. The largest host suite is well inside it (`host/test/dispatcher.test.ts` is 83 lines of code), so the cap is armed here and fires nowhere in this directory; it exists so the suite cannot grow into a single 600-line module while the framework TypeScript profile - which does not report `Lines of Code in a Single File` for `src/agent/graph.ts` at 827 lines of code - stays silent.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The extension's cross-cutting suites: 14 `*.test.ts` files under `tests/` (including `tests/input/` and `tests/page-*.test.ts`), selected by the root `vitest.config.ts` `include: ['tests/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}', ...]`. `tests/` also holds four HTML fixtures (`tests/fixtures/ebay-*.html`, `page-hyperagent-threads.html`) and one support module (`tests/input/support/rng.ts`); the fixtures are not type-checked code and `cs` cannot read `.html` at all, so they are simply out of scope. `tests/page-driver.test.ts` (130 lines of code) is the one suite in this directory that already reports `Code Duplication` on the two screenshot-discard cases at lines 100-111 and 113-123.

rule_sets.rules_doc: Same compliant test profile as `host/test/**`: 20 rules at 1.0, `Low Cohesion`, `Primitive Obsession` and `String Heavy Function Arguments` at 0.0. `tests/page-driver.test.ts` is kept flagged rather than muted - its two near-identical discard cases are the duplication the rule exists to catch, and the fix is one shared case table, not a weight.
rule_sets.thresholds_doc: `file_lines_of_code_for_warning` 500, same as the host suite and for the same reason. The largest file in this directory is `tests/page-driver.test.ts` at 130 lines of code, so the cap does not fire today.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: Every remaining `*.test.ts` suite in the extension: 27 files under `src/` - `src/agent/{graph,tools,policy,grounding,checkpointer}.test.ts`, `src/runtime/{runManager,worker,pageTools,durability,errorLog}.test.ts`, `src/userscripts/{runner,runner.edge,catalog,metadata,match-pattern,debug,authoring,index}.test.ts`, `src/ui/state/*.test.ts`, `src/ui/runlog/format.test.ts`, `src/host/*.test.ts`, `src/input/humanize.test.ts` and `src/stealth/probe.test.ts` - all selected by the root `vitest.config.ts` `include` list. This glob is a filename pattern, so it is deliberately placed after the two directory globs and before every source rule set: a test file never falls through to the application profile of the layer it happens to sit in.

rule_sets.rules_doc: The compliant test profile, unchanged: 20 rules at 1.0, the same three 0.0. The rules that matter here are the ones a coding agent actually trips: `Code Duplication` and `Duplicated Assertion Blocks` already report on `src/runtime/runManager.test.ts`, whose three abort scenarios (lines 319-357, 359-411, 458-512) are the same arrangement of awaits written three times, and `Large Assertion Blocks` keeps a wall of consecutive asserts from hiding which one is the assertion.
rule_sets.thresholds_doc: `file_lines_of_code_for_warning` 500. This is the one cap in the test profile that fires: `src/runtime/runManager.test.ts` is 649 lines of code / 710 physical lines, and it is the reason the number is 500 rather than the framework default. A test module above 500 lines of code is where an agent can no longer find the case it must not break; the refactoring plan splits that module along the seam its own `describe` blocks already draw.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The nine React suite files: `src/ui/components/{ModelSelect,NumberField,Tabs}.test.tsx`, `src/ui/runlog/{RunLog,ToolCallCard,HandoffCard}.test.tsx` and `src/ui/sections/{RunSection,SetupSection,UserscriptsSection}.test.tsx`. They run in jsdom under the root `vitest.config.ts`, and each one asserts rendered output rather than structure. This glob is split from `**/*.test.ts` because `cs` scores the two languages through different parsers and a single `**/*.test.*` glob would not be a valid matching_content_path pattern.

rule_sets.rules_doc: The compliant test profile again, with the same three 0.0 rules. `Primitive Obsession` and `String Heavy Function Arguments` are especially inert on a `.test.tsx` file, whose props are literal JSX; zeroing them here removes a class of false positive without hiding anything structural, because `Complex Method` and `Bumpy Road Ahead` still measure the render helpers a copy-paste grows.
rule_sets.thresholds_doc: `file_lines_of_code_for_warning` 500. `src/ui/sections/SetupSection.test.tsx` is the largest at 361 physical lines and, because `cs` counts JSX markup as neither code nor declaration, well under the cap; the threshold is armed for the future module that is logic-heavy rather than markup-heavy.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The native messaging host's real code: all 22 non-test modules under `host/src/`, of which `llm.ts` (the OpenRouter/Kilo proxy), `secrets.ts` (Doppler resolution with retry), `dispatcher.ts` (the wire router), `protocol.ts` (the normative message types), `trigger.ts` (the dev unix socket), `runlog.ts`, `artifacts.ts`, `framing.ts`, `extlog.ts`, `origins.ts`, `outbound.ts`, `paths.ts`, `log.ts` and `main.ts` are the load-bearing ones, plus `host/src/cli/` (the five `nb-*` commands, `options.ts` and `socket-client.ts`) and `host/src/input/index.ts` (the injector slot). This is the half of the repository that holds the API key, streams model responses and writes to the user's disk - `docs/host-protocol.md` opens by saying 'the native-messaging host **is** the daemon'. It is Node, not browser code, so it is a separate rule set from the extension rather than a subdirectory of one.

rules.name: Lines of Code in a Single File

rule_sets.rules_doc: Nine structural rules at 1.0, none relaxed. `Dispatcher.handle` - the public wrapper at 60-71 plus its private `#handle` at 73-201, which `cs` reports as one function at cc 38 with a 116-line body - covers seven message types plus the four-variant `input.*` union and carries three compound conditionals; that is a real routing seam that should become a table, not a false positive. `llm.ts`, `secrets.ts` and `trigger.ts` already score 8.54, 9.68 and 8.85, so the set is not there to lower numbers - it is there so a future 'temporary' mute in the process that holds the credential is a visible diff in review.
rule_sets.thresholds_doc: `file_lines_of_code_for_warning` 300. Measured: `host/src/llm.ts` is 202 lines of code / 315 physical, `host/src/dispatcher.ts` 162 / 231, `host/src/trigger.ts` 154 / 213, `host/src/protocol.ts` 0 scorable (it is types only - `cs review` returns `score: null`), `host/src/secrets.ts` 131 / 299. A host module above 300 lines of code is where an agent stops being able to hold the whole channel in context, and nothing in `host/src/` is near it today. The framework TypeScript default is far looser - `src/agent/graph.ts` is 827 lines of code and reports no `Lines of Code in a Single File` - so the cap has to be stated explicitly to be real.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The extension's half of the same channel: `src/host/native.ts` (the `HostClient` that speaks `chrome.runtime.connectNative`, maps the model catalog and dispatches host messages - 290 lines of code / 675 physical), plus `fetch.ts` and `redact.ts` and their three suites (which the `**/*.test.ts` glob claims first). It mirrors `host/src/**` on purpose: both sides of the protocol get the same structural guardrail, so a change that widens one end has to answer to the same rules as the other.

rule_sets.rules_doc: Nine structural rules at 1.0. `HostClient.onMessage` (lines 569-644) is cc 26 and `HostClient.listModels` (441-474) is cc 17 with three bumps; `mapCatalogModel` (317-343) is cc 15. Those are the three functions that decide whether a model reply becomes a usable catalog entry, and they are where a wire change is most likely to be bolted on rather than placed. Nothing is relaxed; `src/host/native.ts` scores 8.35 under the framework profile and stays exactly there.
rule_sets.thresholds_doc: `file_lines_of_code_for_warning` 300, the same number as `host/src/**` because it is the same channel. `src/host/native.ts` is at 290 lines of code, so the cap is one growth step away from firing on a 675-physical-line file - which is the point: the next feature added to it produces a finding instead of another 100 lines.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The page world: `actions.ts` (click, hover, type, press, select, scroll, get_box and the humanised pointer path - 1108 physical lines / 612 lines of code), `snapshot.ts` (the accessibility tree that gives every actionable element a `[ref=eNN]` handle), `accname.ts` (accessible-name computation), `driver.ts` (injection, navigation and screenshots), `handler.ts` (the in-page message listener), `extractText.ts`, `tabReplacement.ts` and the `index.ts` barrel. This is the only code that runs inside the user's real page, and `scripts/check-invariants.sh` enforces four structural rules over it so a change cannot reintroduce a detection tell.

rules.name: Lines of Code in a Single File

rule_sets.rules_doc: Nine structural rules at 1.0 and nothing muted. `type` (757-801) is cc 13 with two bumps, `pressTarget` (878-898) cc 14, `barredByDisabledFieldset` (639-657) nests four conditionals deep, and `surrounding context` - four pointer/mouse helpers already take 5 to 7 arguments (`pointerInit` 197, `mouseInit` 227, `pointerAt` 268, `mouseAt` 294) - so `Excess Number of Function Arguments` is doing real work here. A page action that grows a fourth guard is how a humanisation detail silently stops applying on one path.
rule_sets.thresholds_doc: `file_lines_of_code_for_warning` 400. Measured across the directory: `actions.ts` 612 lines of code / 1108 physical, `accname.ts` 258 / 502, `snapshot.ts` 254 / 470, `driver.ts` 210 / 445. The cap fires on exactly one file, `actions.ts`, and that is the intended calibration: one page module has become the whole page layer, and the refactoring plan splits it along the seam its own exported functions already draw. 400 is one step above the largest remaining module, so the rest of the directory has room and `actions.ts` does not.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The LangGraph agent: `graph.ts` (both nodes, the system prompts, the observation compaction, the routing decision - 1284 physical lines / 827 lines of code), `tools.ts` (the toolset the model sees - 777 / 424), `models.ts` (the OpenRouter model handles and the no-`choices` rewrite), `checkpointer.ts` (the IndexedDB saver), `run.ts`, `policy.ts`, `state.ts`, `grounding.ts` and the `index.ts` barrel. `REQUIREMENTS.md` R-03 fixes the Leader/Follower vocabulary and R-04 makes `planningInterval` the re-plan control, so this layer's shape is a stated requirement rather than a style preference.

rules.name: Lines of Code in a Single File

rule_sets.rules_doc: Nine structural rules at 1.0. `graph.ts` is the repository's lowest score at 3.97 and everything it reports is real: `leader` (603-896) is cc 37 / 239 lines with 5 bumps, `follower` (898-1268) is cc 62 / 286 lines with 14 bumps at nesting depth 4, and `followerFeedback` (351-373) and `promptChars` (380-395) each nest four deep. The point of keeping every weight at 1.0 is that the refactoring plan measures itself against this exact report; a muted rule would give the plan nothing to prove.
rule_sets.thresholds_doc: `file_lines_of_code_for_warning` 400. Measured: `graph.ts` 827 lines of code / 1284 physical, `tools.ts` 424 / 777, `checkpointer.ts` 305 / 467, `run.ts` 138 / 243, `models.ts` 117 / 358. The cap fires on `graph.ts` and on `tools.ts` and on nothing else in the directory, and both of those files are targets of .codescene/refactor-action-plan.md, so the finding and the plan agree. 400 is used for this layer and for `src/page/**` alike because both are single-purpose modules an agent must read whole before editing; it is one step above the largest module that is not a target (`checkpointer.ts`, 305), so the boundary is measured rather than picked.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The service-worker runtime: `runManager.ts` (the single run slot, the replay ring and the persistence chain - 748 physical lines / 390 lines of code), `pageTools.ts` (the tool implementations and the tab-rebind adapter - 974 / 526), `worker.ts` (the panel message hub), plus `durability.ts`, `errorLog.ts` and the `index.ts` barrel that `entrypoints/background.ts` imports. This is where four Chrome surfaces - tabs, scripting, debugger and storage - are joined into one run, and it is the layer the panel and the graph both talk to.

rules.name: Lines of Code in a Single File

rule_sets.rules_doc: Nine structural rules at 1.0. `rebindMissingTabDriver` (pageTools 184-272) is cc 28 in 78 lines, `createPageTools.saveFile` (857-933) is cc 24, `RunManager.launch` (runManager 349-595) is cc 45 in 192 lines with two bumps, `RunManager.remember` (656-702) nests four deep, and `createWorker.handlePanelMessage` (worker 224-323) is cc 28 / 95 lines. None of these is a false positive: each one is a place where a new Chrome quirk is appended rather than placed, which is precisely how an agent-authored run loop degrades.
rule_sets.thresholds_doc: `file_lines_of_code_for_warning` 350. Measured: `pageTools.ts` 526 lines of code / 974 physical, `runManager.ts` 390 / 748, `worker.ts` 257 / 460. 350 is the number that makes the runtime set bite on the two files that actually hold the run: both fire. A 400 cap would have let `runManager.ts` - the file that owns the single run slot - pass at 390, which is the wrong signal for the one module whose mistakes drive the user's own tab.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The userscript subsystem: `runner.ts` (execute a script in the `USER_SCRIPT` world, stream its console, enforce the 120 s ceiling and the stop flag - 668 physical lines / 294 lines of code), `catalog.ts` (bundled seeds and stored scripts), `metadata.ts` (the required http/https host declaration), `match-pattern.ts`, `authoring.ts` (the agent's write path), `debug.ts`, `examples.ts`, `ebay-ram.ts` (the one bundled seed that makes requests), `i03.ts`, `index.ts` and `testing.ts`. R-09 and R-10 make live userscripts and live userscript debugging requirements, so this layer ships agent-written code into a page - the highest-consequence surface in the extension after the page actions themselves.

rules.name: Lines of Code in a Single File

rule_sets.rules_doc: Nine structural rules at 1.0. `runUserscript` (434-584) is cc 35 with three bumps in 119 lines, `__nbPush` (235-250) is cc 11, and `runUserscript:565` and `nonJsonReturn:609` each carry two compound conditionals - all of it the shape of an execution path that grew a case per reply the Chrome `userScripts` API can return. A duplicated guard here is a scope escape or a lost timeout, not a style question, so nothing is muted.
rule_sets.thresholds_doc: `file_lines_of_code_for_warning` 300. Measured: `runner.ts` 294 lines of code / 668 physical, `catalog.ts` 119 / 256, `authoring.ts` 74 / 185, `debug.ts` 54 / 148. The cap fires nowhere today, and that is a decision rather than an oversight: `runner.ts` sits four lines of code under 300, and tightening the cap to 250 purely to make it report a size finding would measure the wrong thing. Its debt is one function - `runUserscript` is 119 lines - and `Large Method`, `Complex Method` (cc 35) and `Bumpy Road Ahead` (3 bumps) already report it at full weight. 300 is the bound for the module that executes agent-written code in the user's session: the next userscript file to pass it produces a finding instead of another silent doubling.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: Catch-all, deliberately last. Everything the sets above do not name: `src/ui/**` (49 files, 37 of them `.tsx` - the side panel, run log and state), `src/input/**` (the in-page, debugger/CDP and humanisation tiers), `src/messaging/**` (the typed panel/worker contract), `src/storage/**`, `src/stealth/**`, `entrypoints/**` (the WXT background, injected and side-panel entries), `scripts/**` (the `.sh` drivers and `scripts/harness/*.mjs` scorers), `docs/`, `.github/`, and any directory a future change introduces. All 23 rules are pinned at 1.0 with the framework thresholds for the detected language, so a new directory starts under the full guardrail and has to earn a relaxation with a measured rule set of its own rather than inheriting one. Inputs `cs` cannot read are covered elsewhere: `.sh` drivers by shellcheck and `scripts/check-invariants.sh`, the manifest invariants by the same script, `.md` by review, and the JSON/YAML configs by `pnpm typecheck`.
